full_judgment: 14. Mr. Khan next argued that the plaintiff was a postal peon and presumably knew how to read and write and, as such, it appears that the plaintiff, examined as PW 1, himself stated that he knew how to read and write both the English and the Bengali languages. Mr. Khan wants to say that since the plaintiff himself was a literate man, the natural presumption would be that he had executed the document after knowing the contents of the document. True, the natural presumption of the court is that a literate person who admits execution of the document must be presumed to have executed the document after knowing its contents but the presumption is a rebuttable presumption. Mr. Khan tried to argue with reference to the evidence on record and certain surrounding circumstances that the courts below ought not to have relied on the evidence of PW 1 to the effect that he was unaware of the contents of the document, Unfortunately, this contention of Mr. Khan does not hold good, because we have already seen that the courts below arrived at the finding that the plaintiff had been able to establish by adducing evidence that the document had been obtained without allowing him to know its contents and by practicing fraud. We have already observed that this court cannot enter into the question of the propriety of this finding if this court is satisfied that the said finding by the courts below had been arrived at after proper consideration of the evidence before them. In the ease before us it appears that both the courts below analyzed the oral evidence and documentary evidence placed before them in detail and after detailed analysis came to the conclusion that the defendant got the Hiba-Bil-Ewaz scribbled in the absence of the plaintiff and then represented that it was a deed of mortgage and thereby got it executed and registered by the plaintiff. In view of the reasons stated above, this court cannot interfere with these findings of facts arrived at by the courts below. It, therefore, appears that no error of law was committed by the first appellate Court and the trial Court and it had not also been established that by committing any such error of law the courts below came to any erroneous decision.
